title: Install signal investigation and ops snapshot — private deploys (May 18-20 2026)
body:
Purpose
Summary notes from a focused triage session and three short standups related to repeated "install-signal" failures observed during on-prem and VPC installs for two customers between 2026-05-14 and 2026-05-18. This doc captures observed symptoms, hypotheses, temporary mitigations, action owners, and suggested runbook edits.

High-level impact
- Two active customers (Enterprise A and RetailCo) experienced 10–30% of install attempts failing in the final service-bootstrap phase, producing a transient "signal_loss" marker in agent logs. Customers report long holds (>20 min) or installer aborts, blocking go-live for Dedicated/Private installs.
- Affects both VPC and air-gapped on-prem variants (same installer binary v1.12.0).

Timeline (key events)
- 2026-05-14: Enterprise A initial install cascade: 4/12 installers failed with signal_loss. Ticket: INF-1982 opened by Solutions Eng.
- 2026-05-16: RetailCo run (on-prem, air-gapped) saw intermittent failures; installer retried and succeeded on second attempt.
- 2026-05-17: Telemetry spike detected for installer stage 'service-bootstrap'. Alert rule raised.
- 2026-05-18: Triage call attended by eng-private-deployments, infra, SRE; initial mitigation (backoff + extra logging) rolled to canary.

Standup excerpts (concise logs)
- 2026-05-18 09:15 — Daily deploy standup
  - Marco: Added extended logging around TLS handshake and unix socket open call in agent boot sequence; canary rolling to 2 installs.
  - Sofia: Verified installer v1.12.0 checksum across 5 customer artifacts; all match. Suspect runtime (kernel/net) timing.
  - Aisha: Confirmed alerting surface; created INF-2027 to track telemetry enrichment.

- 2026-05-19 10:00 — Post-canary review
  - Daniel: Canary installs still show 2/10 with signal_loss; trace suggests process waiting on epoll_read for >30s before abort.
  - Priya: Captured verbose strace on failing run — blocking on accept() on control socket until a delayed keepalive from control-plane (~28s).
  - Ethan: Temporary mitigation activated: install now retries control-plane connect with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s) and extended socket timeout to 60s.

- 2026-05-20 09:30 — Sync with SRE (post-mitigation validation)
  - SRE notes: Network device counters (RX drop) correlate with failing installs on a subset of NICs with older firmware.
  - Infra: Filed coordination ticket to vendor for NIC firmware (see linked artifacts).
  - Action: Hold further production rollouts to similar hardware until next validation window.

Observed signals and logs (concise)
- Installer logs snippet (sanitized):
  "[service-bootstrap] waiting for control-plane heartbeat (attempt 1)"
  "[service-bootstrap] epoll_wait timeout=30000ms, returning 0 events"
  "[service-bootstrap] signal_loss detected, aborting installer"
- Strace excerpt (failing case): blocking on accept() and epoll_pwait with timeout; subsequent syscall returns EINTR after 30s.
- Telemetry: sudden increase in socket late-ACKs and retransmits for customer subnets during install windows.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) Network-layer microbursts + older NIC firmware lead to packet drops on small control-plane exchanges; installer currently treats missing heartbeat as fatal. (High confidence)
2) Race in agent control-plane handshake where initial keepalive is delayed under load; lack of jitter/backoff in installer exacerbates failures. (Medium)
3) Edge case: corrupted images or compressed payloads causing longer decompression CPU spikes on low-memory appliances leading to delayed readiness. (Low)

Immediate mitigations applied (and why)
- Exponential backoff + extended socket timeout in installer (temporary patch) — reduces false positives for transient network delays. Deployed as canary to installers for new runs. (Owner: Ethan)
- Enhanced logging (TLS handshake timing, socket-level metrics) to improve signal fidelity for root cause. (Owner: Marco)
- Hold on rolling new installs to customer pods with NIC firmware < 3.2.1 pending vendor patches. (Owner: Sofia)

Recommended long-term fixes
- Installer: change fatal 'signal_loss' to a softer failure mode that triggers auto-retry with full jitter and a configurable max duration. Persist state about partial bootstrap to avoid rework on retry. (Owner: eng-private-deployments)
- Runbook: add explicit preflight NIC firmware check and a fast hardware compatibility probe to detect old NICs and surface to Solutions Eng before install. (Owner: Solutions Engineering)
- Telemetry: add per-install socket-level telemetry (retransmit counts, rtt histograms) exported to Console for per-customer dashboards and alert thresholds. (Owner: observability)

Open action items (owners and ETA)
- INF-1982 (Marco): Synthetic reproduction job that simulates small-packet drops + NIC timing to validate hypothesis. ETA: 2026-05-25.
- INF-2027 (Aisha): Telemetry schema changes merged and backfilled for failing installs (add tcp_retransmits and epoll_wait_durations). ETA: 2026-05-22.
- Runbook update (Priya): Draft NIC firmware preflight checklist and include firmware detection commands (ethtool + vendor-specific). ETA: 2026-05-21.
- Infra coordination (Sofia): Contact NIC vendor and collect firmware test images; escalate if vendor fix timeline >2 weeks. ETA: 2026-05-24.
- Installer patch (Ethan): Promote canary backoff behavior to v1.12.1 and open PR for graceful retry state. ETA: 2026-05-21 (PR link in linked_artifacts).

Notes for customer comms
- For Enterprise A and RetailCo: provide a short summary of root-cause hypothesis, temporary mitigations in place, and expected timeline for permanent fix. Offer assisted re-run with canary-enabled installers and extended socket timeouts.
- Avoid deep technical details about vendor firmware; frame as "network firmware update" coordinated with their infra teams.

Runbook edits (proposed snippets)
- Preflight checks: run ethtool -i <if> to inspect driver/firmware; if firmware < 3.2.1, block and advise vendor upgrade.
- Installer behavior: on service-bootstrap failure, automatically run 3 retries with full jitter and write partial-state to /var/lib/redwood/install-state.json before final failure.

Risks and follow-ups
- Risk: Promoting canary behavior to all customers may mask a deeper timing bug that surfaces under heavy load; keep canary telemetry for 2 weeks and set alert if retry rate >5%.
- Follow-up: schedule cross-team postmortem if permanent fix timeline exceeds 10 business days.

Appendix: useful commands and artifacts
- Check NIC driver/firmware: sudo ethtool -i eth0
- Capture epoll wait stack: sudo perf record -p <pid> -- sleep 10; sudo perf script
- Strace collection: sudo strace -f -tt -o /tmp/installer-strace.log ./install.sh --verbosity debug
- Reproduction harness (internal): scripts/installer-sim/packet-loss-sim (linked in GH PR)

Meeting attendees (Alpha triage call 2026-05-18)
- Aisha Patel (owner, eng-private-deployments)
- Marco Lin (debugging lead)
- Sofia Nguyen (infra)
- Daniel Ortega (SRE)
- Priya Ramesh (solutions eng)
- Ethan Brooks (installer owner)

Summary/next check-in
- Next sync scheduled: 2026-05-22 09:30 PT to review telemetry from promoted canary and vendor firmware response. If telemetry shows retry rate <2% and NIC vendor provides patch timeline <2 weeks, we proceed with rolling to queued installs.

End of document.
